questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Makes sure oil lubricates the engine properly.
Stops the tractor from going too fast.
Keeps air in the truck's braking system if the trailer leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the truck's braking system if the trailer leaks.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck's braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. The valve closes automatically if air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer, what should you do next?
questions.explanation: When coupling trailers, the correct steps are important for safe operation. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, you should supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer straight, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: If you cannot back your trailer straight, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: When braking a trailer with anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Use extra braking force to make sure the brakes work.
Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.
questions.explanation: With anti-lock brakes, brake the same way you would if the vehicle did not have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, where should the air supply control lever be?
questions.explanation: The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when pulling a trailer. This is the correct setting for safe operation.

questions.question: What does rearward amplification mean?

options.text: The amount of noise at the back of a vehicle.
How many trailers a tractor can pull.

questions.explanation: Trailers can tip over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect, which is caused by rearward amplification.

questions.question: How should cargo be loaded to prevent a rollover?

options.text: Load most weight on the driver's side of the trailer.
Place weight near the rear of the trailer.
Spread weight evenly throughout the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread weight evenly throughout the trailer.
questions.explanation: Spread cargo weight evenly in the trailer to prevent rollover. Do not put too much weight on one side.

questions.question: When pulling trailers, what should you do?

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Push the accelerator to the floor when starting.

questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: When backing up to couple the tractor to a trailer, what should you do with the trailer brakes?
questions.explanation: Before backing the tractor under the trailer while coupling, lock the trailer brakes.

questions.question: When braking with anti-lock brakes, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: With anti-lock brakes, apply the brakes the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line supply air to?
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks. It also controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: What happens when a combination vehicle goes around a corner?

options.text: The vehicle must use at least two lanes.
The front and rear wheels will move in different paths.
It is best to allow the rear wheels to drive over the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels will move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle goes around a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. This effect is stronger on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors attached to full semitrailers.
questions.explanation: Bobtail tractors are tractors not attached to any semitrailer. When driving a bobtail, know that stopping is harder. It will take longer to stop than a tractor attached to a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has ____ air line(s).
questions.explanation: Every combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: Rearward amplification refers to:

options.text: The amount of noise projected to the rear of the vehicle.
The number of trailers that can be pulled by one tractor.

questions.explanation: The "crack-the-whip" effect happens because of rearward amplification. If not handled properly, a trailer can tip over due to rearward amplification.

questions.question: If the trailer begins to drift while backing, the driver should:

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer begins to drift while backing, correct it right away. Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, you should:

options.text: Couple together the proper glad hands.
Couple glad hands with any other glad hands.
Leave one pair of glad hands loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Couple together the proper glad hands.
questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are sometimes color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
Glad hands can be connected to any other glad hands.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to couple the proper glad hands.
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, you should ensure that the:
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air reaches all air brakes on all trailers. Open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves and listen for air escaping. Close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must be equipped with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
